en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Seventh Chapter
The Discourse on the Ripening of Noble Qualities:
Is there no ripening of noble qualities? Yes, [there is].
Affirmative.
Is it not the case that the state of a recluse (sāmañña) is of great fruit and the state of a brahmin (brahmañña) is of great fruit?
Yes, it is.
If the state of a recluse is of great fruit and the state of a brahmin is of great fruit, then indeed, you should not say: [that they are not so].
“There is no fruition of the noble Dhamma.
Is it the case that there is no fruition of the noble Dhamma?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that there is the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes, it is.
If indeed there is the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you should not say:
“There is no ripening of the noble Dhamma.
Is it not the case that there is the fruit of once-returning …pe… the fruit of non-returning …pe…?
Is there the fruit of arahantship? Yes.
If there is the fruit of arahantship, then indeed, it should not be said—
“There is no ripening of the noble dhamma.
Is the fruit of stream-entry not a ripening? Yes.
Is the fruit of giving not a result of maturation?
One should not say so …pe… Is the fruit of stream-entry not a result of maturation?
“Yes.
“Is the fruit of virtue … [and so on] … the fruit of development not a result (vipāka)?”
It should not be stated thus … [and so on] … the fruit of once-returning … the fruit of non-returning … [and so on].
Is the fruit of arahantship not a result of karmic ripening?
Yes. Is the fruit of giving not a result of karmic ripening?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the fruit of arahantship not a result of maturation (vipāka)? Yes.
Is the fruit of virtue …pe… the fruit of development not a result (vipāka)?
One must not say so …pe…
Is the fruit of giving a result of maturation?
Yes. Is the fruit of stream-entry a result of maturation? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the fruit of giving a result of karmic ripening? Yes.
Is the fruit of once-returning …pe… the fruit of non-returning …pe… the fruit of arahantship a result (vipāka)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the fruit of virtue … [as before] … the fruit of development a result (vipāka)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the fruit of stream-entry a result (vipāka)?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is the fruit of cultivation (bhāvanāphala) a result of karmic ripening (vipāka)? Yes. Is the fruit of the once-returner (sakadāgāmiphala) [a result of karmic ripening]? Yes. ... [and so on] ...
Is the fruit of non-returning …pe… the fruit of arhatship a result of karmic ripening?
One should not say so …pe….
Is wholesome [kamma] of the sense sphere accompanied by result?
Yes. Is supramundane wholesome [kamma] accompanied by result? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … Is wholesome consciousness of the fine-material sphere …pe… wholesome consciousness of the immaterial sphere accompanied by result?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is supramundane wholesome [kamma] with result?
You should not say so … [as before] … .
Is supramundane wholesome [kamma] without result? Yes.
Is sense-sphere wholesome [kamma] without result? No.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is supramundane wholesome [kamma] without fruition? Yes.
Is the wholesome [kamma] of the fine-material sphere …pe… the wholesome [kamma] of the immaterial sphere without result?
One should not say so …pe….
Is wholesome consciousness of the sense sphere (kāmāvacara) accompanied by result and leading to accumulation?
Yes. Is supramundane (lokuttara) wholesome consciousness accompanied by result and leading to accumulation? No.
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … Is the wholesome of the fine-material sphere … and the wholesome of the immaterial sphere accompanied by result and leading to accumulation?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is supramundane wholesome [kamma] with result that leads to accumulation?
You should not say so … [as before].
Is supramundane wholesome [kamma] with result that leads to diminution? Yes.
Is sense-sphere wholesome [kamma] with result that leads to diminution?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is supramundane wholesome karma accompanied by result and leading to dispersal? Yes.
Is the wholesome consciousness of the fine-material sphere …pe… the wholesome consciousness of the immaterial sphere, which has a result and leads to diminution,
[to be called] "leading to dispersal"? One should not say so …pe….
The Discussion on the Ripening of Noble Dhamma is finished.
